items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: It almost sounded like you were thinking of J.S. Bach. I’ve been trying to get a contrapuntal way of playing going and it’s coming along.

ctx.x: the economics were different, that there were staff orchestras where you could be working for a pretty decent weekly salary as a staff musician. Those don’t exist anymore. There were staff orchestras in California — the film studios had their own orchestras — MGM for example. And live music was everywhere. There were always live bands playing or at least pianists or least organists or at least something playing everywhere you looked. This was very different from now, when most music you hear is synthesized or…

I have to tell you that today the solo you played on, was it “Crazy Rhythm” I’m still trying to figure out what you were doing in your left hand while you were — it almost sounded like you were thinking of J.S. Bach. Do you consciously think of —
I’ve been trying to get a contrapuntal way of playing going and it’s coming along.
